description: termination_notice_band for contract cleaning Area B under the BCCCI Main Agreement, clause 21.1(b), in three rows rather than four (D-315). The six-month limit in the probation limb is the instrument's own words and is kept in its citation, but it never binds: clause 3 caps probation at four months, so no employee is on probation at six months, and off probation the notice is two weeks on both sides of six months. So the boundary at six months changed no answer, and the restructure was loaded only after every reachable answer was proven unchanged. Supersedes r4, whose rows are kept. NOT verified.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Bargaining Council for the Contract Cleaning Services Industry (KZN) Main Collective Agreement, GN R.7296 in GG 54412, 27 March 2026, clause 21.1(b)(i)
termination_notice_band.notes: One WORKING day, so the unit is days and nothing here converts it to a fraction of a week - contract cleaning runs six-day weeks and a day is worth a sixth of one, not a fifth (D-68). Clause 21.2(a)(i) prices it at the daily wage being received at the time of termination. BCEA s37(2)(a) and s49(1) pull different ways on this band and the question is OPEN (D-316, referred to the labour law review, O-06): s37(1)(a) requires one week's notice for six months' service or less and s37(2)(a) says 'a collective agreement may not permit a notice period shorter than that required by subsection (1)'; but s49(1) lets a bargaining council agreement 'alter, replace or exclude any basic condition of employment' subject to exceptions that do not include notice, and s49(2) is what confines OTHER collective agreements. This is the only band below s37(1). Loaded exactly as the instrument states it: there is no 'safer' fallback, because notice is symmetric and there is no safe direction. SD1 clause 23(1)(a) gives the same one working day in the first four weeks, so the answer governs both sectors.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Bargaining Council for the Contract Cleaning Services Industry (KZN) Main Collective Agreement, GN R.7296 in GG 54412, 27 March 2026, clause 21.1(b), 'ii)' as published
termination_notice_band.notes: "Not less than one weeks notice shall be given to an employee whilst on probation, as defined, for the period of employment between 4 weeks as in sub clause (i) above and six months" - verbatim, as printed on gazette page 36. THE EXCEPTION for a named class (D-277). The band is open-ended where the clause says 'and six months' because the six months never binds: clause 3 caps probation at four months and employees/probation.py refuses a longer one at engagement, so every employee on probation is inside the window. The restructure loader proved no reachable answer moved (D-315); if clause 3 is ever amended beyond six months, this band must be split again, and statutory/tests/test_notice_restructure.py pins the loaded cap at no more than six months so that cannot happen silently. NO PAYMENT-IN-LIEU FIGURE: clause 21.2(a) prices only the one working day and the two weeks; BCEA s38(1) pays the remuneration the employee would have received under s35 for the notice period, one week here, which calculators/termination.py already does for every band.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Bargaining Council for the Contract Cleaning Services Industry (KZN) Main Collective Agreement, GN R.7296 in GG 54412, 27 March 2026, clause 21.1(b), second 'i)' as published
termination_notice_band.notes: "Not less than two weeks notice shall be given after the first four weeks of such employment". THE GENERAL RULE, qualified by nothing, so it governs every employee not on probation from four weeks on, before six months and after it alike - which is why the six-month boundary r4 carried changed no figure (D-315). The published numbering repeats 'i)'; this is the second one. Clause 21.2(a)(ii) prices it at double the weekly wage being received at the time of termination.
